title: Copilot Studio: block maker-provided credentials for tool authentication
summary: Hold: the maker-side tool authentication route combines a section from the connector instructions with a setting label from a different route. The current cited page places Authentication directly under Details. The default, enforcement effects and roadmap facts are supported, but the licensing model also understates published product-level requirements.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Control maker credential options lets administrators block maker-provided credentials for agent tools.
claims.quote: Admins can enable and disable the selection of maker-provided credentials in the Power Platform admin center, as described in this article.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A connector or Power Automate flow tool configured with maker credentials authenticates as the maker for agent users.
claims.quote: When someone uses the agent, the agent uses the maker's credentials, not the end user's credentials, to authenticate with connected services.

claims.claim: Administrators can allow end-user credentials, maker-provided credentials, or both.
claims.quote: You choose whether makers can select to use their own credentials for authenticating tool connections, to use the end-user's credentials, or to have access to both.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in: both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled by default, with no restriction until configured.
claims.quote: By default, both End-user and Maker-provided credentials are enabled.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; controls[0].note; Why it matters
claims.claim: Restricting maker-provided credentials immediately removes the maker's ability to select them.
claims.quote: When configured as instructed, the feature immediately turns off the maker's ability to select their credentials for authenticating tools within the environment or environment group.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking maker-provided credentials changes all tools for all agents in affected environments to end-user authentication at run time.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users in new conversations with affected agents are prompted to sign in to the connected service if needed.
claims.quote: Enforcing the use of end-user credentials prompts the end user to sign in (to the relevant service or connector) when needed.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The credential control is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments (or Environment groups) > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.
claims.quote: In the environment's details page, select Settings on the top menu bar. Expand the Product section, and select Features. ... Scroll to the Copilot Studio agents section. ... Under Control maker credential options, select End-user credentials or Maker-provided credentials, or both.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: No PowerShell, REST, Power Platform API or pac CLI operation is documented for the credential-option control.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" Power Platform API PowerShell pac admin Dataverse setting; "Control maker credential options" "API"; read configure-no-maker-authentication and pac admin search excerpts; no operation or deciding property found.

claims.claim: Environment Admin is the documented role for configuring the credential option in a single environment.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: Power Platform Administrator or Global Admin is the documented role for configuring the credential option for environment groups.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin permissions (Environment Admin for a single environment, or Power Platform Administrator/Global Admin for environment groups).

claims.claim: An environment in a group requires a tenant admin with access to that group to configure this control.
claims.quote: If the environment you want to configure is part of an environment group, you must be a tenant admin with access to the group.

claims.claim: For a grouped environment, administrators must configure the credential option on the group's details page rather than the environment's individual page.
claims.quote: You can't configure this feature on the individual details page for environments that are in a group, you must use the group's details page.

claims.claim: Environment group settings override individual environment settings, whose credential options become unavailable.
claims.quote: If the environment is in a group, the options are unavailable and a message directs you to configure the setting for the group, not the individual environment. ... environment group settings override any environment settings.

claims.claim: The credential policy applies to existing and new agents in the selected environment or environment group.
claims.quote: Choose whether end-user or maker credentials (or both) can be selected by makers for agents in an environment, or for all agents in all environments in an environment group. ... Once active, all existing and new agents in that environment adhere to this rule.

claims.claim: When maker credentials are blocked, each tool call must authenticate with a live user sign-in.
claims.quote: When maker-provided credentials are prevented from being used, agents require real-time user interaction because each tool call must be authenticated with a live user sign-in.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Learn warns that scheduled-event agents fail due to missing credentials when maker-provided credentials are blocked.
claims.quote: As a result, agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn warns that agents attempting to run in the background fail due to missing credentials when maker-provided credentials are blocked.
claims.quote: As a result, agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.claim: No stored maker credentials are used at run time when end-user credentials are enforced.

claims.claim: Learn documents no other credential type that remains available under this maker-credential block.
claims.quote: Searched: "Control maker credential options" exemption exception MCP; read configure-no-maker-authentication and configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials. The latter permits system identities under sharing enforcement, not an exception to the credential-option block.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Enforcing end-user credentials restricts actions and data access to permissions the end user's account has.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity. If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Makers whose tools previously used their credentials might be prompted to change the configuration before publishing.
claims.quote: If the maker previously had a tool configured with their credentials, they might be prompted to change it before publishing the agent.

claims.claim: The authentication-type control covers connectors, built-in actions and embedded Power Automate flows equally.
claims.quote: The control over the authentication type covers connectors, built-in actions, and embedded Power Automate flows equally.

claims.claim: For a Power Automate flow used as an agent tool, each user signs in for the connections the flow uses.
claims.quote: A Power Automate flow as a tool in the agent also requires each user to sign in for any connections that flow uses.

claims.claim: The environment sharing control is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure. ... Select Settings, and then select Features. ... Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation is documented for the environment-level embedded-maker-credential sharing control.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials" Power Platform API PowerShell pac admin settings. Read configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials and Power Apps PowerShell search excerpts; no setting operation found.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: The separate sharing control governs publishing and sharing rather than blocking an agent at run time.
claims.quote: The sharing agents with embedded maker credentials control governs sharing and publishing. It doesn't block an agent while the agent is running.

claims.claim: Enabling sharing enforcement does not retroactively unshare existing agents.
claims.quote: Enabling enforcement doesn't retroactively unshare or disable agents that were previously shared.

claims.claim: The environment sharing control has All sharing allowed and Safe sharing enforced modes.
claims.quote: To provide detection and guidance without blocking, select All sharing allowed. Or, to block unsafe sharing paths, select Safe sharing enforced.

claims.claim: All sharing allowed can be used to assess which agents rely on unsafe embedded maker credentials before enforcement.
claims.quote: Start in a development or validation environment and select All sharing allowed. Use the resulting guidance to understand which agents and flows rely on embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: The Security sharing route is Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials > Environment groups (or Environments) > target > Set up.
claims.quote: On the navigation pane, select Security, and then select Threat detection. ... Select Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials. A panel opens. ... Select Set up.
claims.fix: The route stops on the right setup page but before the setting. Extend it to 'Security > Threat detection > Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials > Environment groups (or Environments) > environment group (or environment) > Set up > Don't let makers share agents with their own credentials embedded (recommended)' as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/security/control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials.

claims.claim: No API or automation operation is documented for the Security sharing control at environment or environment-group scope.
claims.quote: Searched: "Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials" "API" "environment"; "maker" "credentials" "Power Platform API" settings. Read security/control-sharing-agents-with-embedded-maker-credentials, environment-groups and pac admin excerpts; no operation setting this control found.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The maker-side authentication field is at Copilot Studio > Tools > tool > Details > Additional details > Authentication.
claims.quote: The configuration page has three sections: Details, Inputs, and Completion. ... Authentication | Runs the tool with the user's credentials (End user, the default) or the maker's credentials (Maker-provided).
claims.fix: Replace controls[3].ui.path and the rendered route with 'Agents > agent > Tools > tool > Details > Authentication'. The cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/add-tools-custom-agent places Authentication directly in Details. Do not insert Additional details from the connector-specific route: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/advanced-connectors instead calls that field 'Credentials to use' under 'Details > Additional details' on the connector tool Overview page.

claims.claim: The maker-side tool authentication default is End user.
claims.quote: Authentication | Runs the tool with the user's credentials (End user, the default) or the maker's credentials (Maker-provided).
